newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX crude ends higher after storm cuts output.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX crude ends higher after storm cuts output.

text.p: NYMEX crude prices ended higher Tuesday on news that Tropical Storm Josephine cut output in some fields and closed ports in the Gulf of Mexico.
"The port situation had to have lent support since it will tighten supplies," said a trader in Texas.
November crude ended 30 cents higher at $25.54 a barrel. Crude hit a session high of $25.60, 10 cents shy of the post-Gulf War high hit last April.
Traders estimated 600,000 barrels were lost in crude output after Josephine swept through the Gulf of Mexico over the weekend.
Josephine disrupted shipping at the deepwater Louisiana Offshore Oil Port and closed two major Mexican terminals, Pajaritos and Dos Bocas.

Josephine has since turned into a cold front moving over the U.S. East Coast. However, traders said the storm cut output in fields operated by such major players like British Petroleum, Mobil, and Chevron.

Meanwhile, November heating oil settled off 0.30 cent a gallon at 76.19 cents and November gasoline settled 0.16 cent higher at 66.50 ahead of weekly oil inventory data expected from the American Petroleum Institute.

"There is a pattern that the market runs up the four (trading) days before every Tuesday, with heating oil ending about unchanged that day to minimize risk," said Ed Kevelson, director of refined products at Paribas Futures Inc.
-- Harry Milling, New York Energy Desk, 212-859-1761
